page.title: Undefined behaviour
page.desc: Operations the C standard deliberately leaves unspecified (signed overflow, out-of-bounds access, data races). Compilers may assume they never happen, which enables optimisation and produces surprising code.
page.intro: Operations the C standard deliberately leaves unspecified (signed overflow, out-of-bounds access, data races). Compilers may assume they never happen, which enables optimisation and produces surprising code.

synapses.text: UB lets the compiler assume programs are well-formed; the cost is that a single overflow can make an optimiser delete a bounds check.
AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instrument builds to report UB as it happens.

parent.title: C
parent.desc: Dennis Ritchie's language from Bell Labs (1972), in which Unix was rewritten in 1973; manual memory management, pointers, and a standard (C89 through C23) that leaves much behaviour undefined on purpose.

synapses.text: UB lets the compiler assume programs are well-formed; the cost is that a single overflow can make an optimiser delete a bounds check.
AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instrument builds to report UB as it happens.
